newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Germany late to enact rules on shellfish waters.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Germany late to enact rules on shellfish waters.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found Germany late to enact the EU directive on the quality of fresh water protection to support fish life.

The German government did not deny that articles 3 and 5 of the directive were not fully implemented by Germany's regional Laenders, but rejected the Commission's view that non-implementation could endanger human life.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Failure by a member state to fulfil obligation - Quality of fresh waters needing protection or improvement in order to support fish life"
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for a declaration that, by failing to adopt within the periods prescribed all the measures necessary to comply with article 3 and 5 of Council directive 78/659/EEC of 18 July 1978 on the quality of fresh waters needing protection or improvement in order to support fish life (OJ 1978 L 222, p. 1) and articles 3 and 5 of Council directive 79/923/EEC of 30 October 1979 on the quality required of shellfish waters (OJ 1979 L 281, p. 47), the Federal Republic of Germany has failed to fulfil its obligations

1. Declares that, by failing to adopt within the periods prescribed all the measures necessary to comply with article 3 and 5 of Council directive 78/659/EEC of 18 July 1978 on the quality of fresh waters needing protection or improvement in order to support fish life and articles 3 and 5 of Council directive 79/923/EEC of 30 October 1979 on the quality required of shellfish waters the Federal Republic of Germany has failed to fulfil its obligations.
2. Orders the Federal Republic of Germany to pay the costs.
